MONDAY - MARCH 20, 2017 - CITY HALL -

COUNCIL CHAMBERS, BLOOMFIELD AVENUE AT 183RD STREET
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.

MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT HELD ON MARCH 20,
2017, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125 BLOOMFIELD
AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Pastor Paul Hansen, First Christian Reformed
  Church of Artesia.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was given by Campfire Long Beach Council.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in
  attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Carol Chen
  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Mark E. Pulido
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Naresh Solanki
  Mayor/Chair George Ray

5.  Presentations/Appointments

  Proclamations presented to:

  State Farm Insurance (Business Spotlight)

  Mickey Christiason (Cerritos Sheriff’s Station/Community Safety Center
  Volunteer of the Year)

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Tom Tislow invited the community to various “Welcome Home Vietnam Veterans”
  events scheduled for March 30, 2017.

7.  Consent Calendar
  Items under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by
  one motion. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless a
  Council/Agency Member or citizen so requests, in which event the item will be
  removed from the Consent Calendar and considered separately.

7A.  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of March
  9, 2017 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated March 20, 2017 in the amount

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray

  ABSTAIN:  None

7C.  Award of Bid No. 1288-17, printing of the Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts

  Season Brochure to Southwest Offset Printing in the amount of $116,948.74. The
  motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray

  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to receive and file

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  Friendship and Brookhaven parks, Project No. 10073, Bid No. 1291-17
  (COUNCIL).

  At the direction of Council this item was removed from the agenda.

8.  Public Hearings

8A.  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF
  THE CITY OF CERRITOS APPROVING PRECISE PLAN 88-1(A)(2017)
  AMENDMENT, A REQUEST BY MGP IX LINCOLN STN, LLC, TO CONVERT AN
  EXISTING RETAIL SPACE INTO A SUPERMARKET USE, TO UPGRADE THE
  EXTERIOR FAÇADE OF THE EXISTING BUILDINGS, AND TO REFURBISH AND
  UPGRADE THE EXISTING LANDSCAPING, BUSINESS IDENTIFICATION SIGNS,
  AND HARDSCAPE AT THE LINCOLN STATION SHOPPING CENTER. THE
  SUBJECT PROPERTY IS LOCATED AT 11900 SOUTH STREET, CERRITOS,
  CALIFORNIA, 90703 AND IS ZONED COMMUNITY COMMERCIAL (CC) (APNS
  7054-024-060 AND 7054-024-061) (COUNCIL).*

  *Pursuant to Section 15301 of the California Environmental Quality Act
  (CEQA), this project is categorically exempt from CEQA Review.

  A staff report was given by Robert A. Lopez, Current Planning Manager. A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  Taylor Pham, representing the applicant, spoke regarding the project and
  timeline.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed
  public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Solanki, to:

  1. Waive full reading of and adopt Resolution No. 2017-5, A RESOLUTION OF
  THE CITY OF CERRITOS APPROVING PRECISE PLAN 88-1(A)(2017)
  AMENDMENT, A REQUEST BY MGP IX LINCOLN STN, LLC, TO CONVERT
  AN EXISTING RETAIL SPACE INTO A SUPERMARKET USE, TO UPGRADE
  THE EXTERIOR FAÇADE OF THE EXISTING BUILDINGS, AND TO
  REFURBISH AND UPGRADE THE EXISTING LANDSCAPING, BUSINESS
  IDENTIFICATION SIGNS, AND HARDSCAPE AT THE LINCOLN STATION
  SHOPPING CENTER. THE SUBJECT PROPERTY IS LOCATED AT 11900
  SOUTH STREET, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA, 90703 AND IS ZONED
  COMMUNITY COMMERCIAL (CC) (APNS 7054-024-060 AND 7054-024-
  061) (COUNCIL). The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of City participation in social media (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Laurie Kajiwara, Public Information Manager. A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments.

  Sally Havice recommended the City partner with local education to provide this
  service.

  Anshuman Sinha spoke regarding suggestions to reduce the service cost and
  managing content.
 City of Cerritos  March 20, 2017
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 4 of 7

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9A.  (continued)

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed public
  comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Chen, and seconded by Pulido, to:
  1.  Direct staff to establish a social media presence.
  2.  Direct staff to take the following actions:
  a. Claim the official City of Cerritos Facebook page.
  b. Develop and post a City of Cerritos Facebook page policy that
  incorporates the language in the CCPA Facebook comments policy.
  c. Develop and implement a protocol for reviewing and responding to posts
  as appropriate.  Basic informational questions would be answered
  immediately with accurate facts while responses to more complicated or
  sensitive comments would require review and approval by the City
  Manager.
  d. Promote the City’s Facebook page through the City’s other media channels,
  including the City’s website, newsletter, e-mail/text message service and
  cable television channel.
  e. Direct staff to research other social media outlets which, if found to provide
  value to the City and the public, will then be added to the list of authorized
  social media sites on which the City can participate.
  The motion carried (4 - 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki
  NOES:  Ray
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review of a settlement agreement between the City of Cerritos, the Successor

  of California Department of Finance (DOF) relating to the resolution of disputed
  enforceable obligations on the Successor Agency’s recognized obligation payment

  Review of the Successor Agency to the Cerritos Redevelopment Agency’s sale of
  various properties identified within the approved long-range property management
  plan to the City of Cerritos and authorization for the expenditure of funds by the
  City of Cerritos to facilitate the purchase of the referenced properties (APNS 7030-

  7030-001-031, 7030-001-033, 7030-001-037, 7030-001-038, 7030-001-040
  through 7030-001-042, 7030-011-004 through 7030-011-012, 7034-018-901 AND
  7034-016-910) (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  A staff report was given by Mark Steres, City Attorney.

  The Mayor opened public comments.

  Jay Gray spoke regarding the future sale of the properties.

  Sally Havice expressed her support for the settlement.

  Anantha Ramachandran spoke regarding placing money back into reserves.
 City of Cerritos  March 20, 2017
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 5 of 7

9.  New and Old Business

9B.  (continued)

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed public
  comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Chen, to:

  1.  Authorize the execution of the Settlement Agreement by the City Manager and
  Executive Director (City/Successor Agency); and,
  2.  Waive full reading of and adopt Resolution No. 2017-6, A RESOLUTION OF
  THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS APPROVING THE

  024-061, 7030-001-020, 7030-001-021, 7030-001-024 through 7030-
  001-027, 7030-001-029 through 7030-001-031, 7030-001-033, 7030-
  001-037, 7030-001-038, 7030-001-040 through 7030-001-042, 7030-
  011-004 through 7030-011-012, 7034-018-901 AND 7034-016-910)
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).
  3.  Authorize the City Council to draft and distribute a letter to all residents and
  businesses in Cerritos outlining the approved settlement agreement.

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9C.  Review and consideration of an informational report on recent storm-related
  damage in the City of Cerritos (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kanna Vancheswaran, Director of Public Works. A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments.

  Jennifer Pilapil spoke regarding budgeting for removal of trees, maintenance, and
  utilizing GIS resources.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed public
  comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to receive and file
  the report (COUNCIL). The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Chen, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9.  New and Old Business

9D.  Review and consideration of candidate forums related to the upcoming April 11,

9E.  Review and consideration of the response received from the request for
  proposals (RFP) for the operation and management of the Cerritos Center for
  the Performing Arts (CCPA) (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kathy Matsumoto, Assistant City Manager.

  The Mayor opened public comments.

  Sally Havice expressed concern regarding community support for subsidizing the
  Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts.

  Jay Gray spoke regarding improving the success of the Cerritos Center for the
  Performing Arts and the economic impact study.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed public
  comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Chen, to receive and file the
  report (COUNCIL). The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
